ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are three JK flip-flops in the figure, labeled FF2, FF1, and FF0 respectively, corresponding to outputs Q2, Q1, and Q0. The clock terminals of the three flip-flops are all connected to the same CP line, so it is a synchronous counter. In the figure, it can also be seen that an upper NAND gate sends high-order feedback signals to the excitation terminal of FF0, and another NAND gate at the lower left together with the feedback lines of each Q and inverted Q jointly determines the J/K excitation of FF1 and FF2. Reasoning: According to the feedback connections in the figure, the excitation conditions can be equivalently written: FF0 toggles when Q2·Q1 is not 1, that is, J0=K0=¬(Q2·Q1); the equivalent excitation of FF1 can be taken as J1=Q0, K1=Q0+Q2; the equivalent excitation of FF2 is J2=Q1·Q0, K2=Q1·¬Q0. Using the JK flip-flop characteristic equation Q+=J·¬Q+¬K·Q, calculate beat by beat from the initial state 000: 000 → 001; 001 → 010; 010 → 011; 011 → 100; 100 → 101; 101 → 110; when 110, FF0 is inhibited by Q2Q1=11 and holds 0, while FF1 and FF2 reset, so 110 → 000. Thus the different states in the cycle are 000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, 110, a total of 7, and 111 does not enter this cycle. Therefore this synchronous up counter is modulo 7.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the circuit contains three JK flip-flops FF2, FF1, FF0 clocked together by CP, so it is a synchronous 3-bit counter. A plain 3-bit up-counter would count modulo 8. Then inspect the NAND feedback: the gate driven by Q2 and Q1 disables the normal setting/toggling of Q0 when the high bits are both 1, and the companion feedback forces the high bits to return so that after count 110 the next state is 000 instead of 111. Therefore exactly one of the eight possible 3-bit states is skipped. Since the text says the initial state is 000, the reachable addition-counting cycle has 8 − 1 = 7 states, so the modulus is 7.
